Notice most of the people in this thread don't care about ads that don't do a few fairly specific things.

These things include not being vectors for malware, not interfering with the content (especially through huge splash screens or forced videos), not interfering with the operation of the browser (e.g. pop-ups), not providing blatantly fraudulent and deceptive ads (e.g. for fake anti-virus software that's really a botnet client) and not dumping sound and video on your head.

Really, it's NOT that hard. Advertisers and web sites just don't give a shit, at least, unless they're forced to, and mass adoption of ad blockers is the only way to do that. But now they've got the odds and popular opinion stacked against them, and they're going to have to shovel through that.

In terms of content being hijacked by corporate interests, while that will of course happen (it does already), I wouldn't be a bit surprised if they found themselves working in an arena that is rather different when volunteers get into the mix, many of whom tend to be area experts. It certainly isn't perfect (a lot of experts aren't and a lot of people who mouth off on the Internet aren't experts), but it's a start.
